title: A Harbor for the Regiment
premise: In 1848, on the eve of revolution in a Rhineland river town, Beatrix Pemberton works her father's type foundry, cutting matrices and keeping the shop's ledger of debts, births, and grievances. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the ledger as evidence, she realizes the names inside it—including her own family's hidden past as refugees—will be rewritten or erased by the victors' historians. Over ten days of occupation, she smuggles the type, the matrices, and the truth itself out in plain sight, printing a clandestine broadsheet that forces the new regime to acknowledge the record. She survives by surrendering the shop but keeps the inheritance that matters: the names, and a town that finally claims her as one of its own.
about_author: Wendell Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing requisitioned records from nineteenth-century European towns. He writes from a converted bindery on the coast, where he still sets type by hand.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the print shop on the eve of revolution, Beatrix cuts a new matrix while her father tallies the ledger of the town's debts, births, and quiet grudges. She measures her life in what fits in a satchel. Emotional beat: tender unease, the calm before requisition.

chapters.title: Orders in Triplicate
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Soldiers arrive with requisition orders: the town's records, ledgers, and presses are seized for the provisional authority. Her father resists and is detained. Beatrix hides one ledger—the one with the names—in the type cabinet. Emotional beat: shock hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Knows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with a flashback to her mother's voice. Reading the hidden ledger, Beatrix confronts the entry revealing her family arrived as undocumented refugees, pardoned by a clerk who is now a collaborator. Emotional beat: the discovery that invisibility was always a story someone told for her.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She visits Herr Vogel, the old clerk turned regime functionary, who offers to restore her father's freedom if she surrenders the ledger and her silence. She refuses but learns the historians arrive in ten days to 'regularize' the record. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into a deadline.

chapters.title: Ten Days of Type
chapters.summary: Alternating Beatrix and her father's prison letters. She plans to print a broadsheet of the true names using smuggled matrices, enlisting the baker's son Anton and the widow Krämer. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, the first taste of belonging through shared risk.

chapters.title: A Search by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A midnight search of the shop nearly uncovers the ledger; Anton distracts the sergeant at cost of a beating. Beatrix sets the first lines of type by candlelight, hands shaking. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into craft—the act of setting type as defiance.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historian
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The regime historian, a courteous man named Albrecht, interviews her and offers to include her family 'kindly' in the official record if the ledger is destroyed. She recognizes the seduction of a clean story. Emotional beat: temptation and clarity—she sees the price of survival plainly.

chapters.title: Night Press
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Anton's alternating POV. They print two hundred broadsheets in the cellar while soldiers billet overhead. The widow Krämer distributes them through the market. By dawn, the true names are on every door. Emotional beat: exhilARATION and exposure—the town can no longer pretend not to know.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Customhouse
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Summoned before Albrecht and Vogel, Beatrix trades the ledger's location for her father's release and a public reading of the names, betting that the town's visible outrage makes erasure costlier than truth. Emotional beat: the climax—she stakes everything on belonging being stronger than fear.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Regiment
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, one year later. The shop reopens under her name; the ledger is copied into the town archive with her as custodian, and the regiment that once requisitioned the town now musters in its square, reading the names aloud each spring. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—inheritance kept, belonging chosen.
